full_judgment: 3. Defendant Nos. 4-9 contested the suit by filing a written statement denying the material statements made in the plaint. Their case, in short, is that Gopal Mondal was the owner of the suit land of CS khatian No. 114 in CS Plot No. 78 measuring an area of 1.06 acres of land. During SA operation 1.16 acres of land of plot No. 78 were recorded in the name of Gurudas Mistiri. While in possession of the suit land, Gurudas Mistri gifted 0.60 acre of land out of 1.16 acres of land to his sister Srimoti Sudhamoni by a registered deed dated 23-1-1947. After that, Sudhamoni transferred her share in favour of Ahmed Hossain and Nur Mohammad by a registered deed dated 01-5-1950. Meanwhile, the Government acquired 7 decimals of land from suit plot No. 78 pursuant to LA Case No. 13/1967-1968 for construction of Dhaka-Narayangonj Link Road and remaining 51 decimals of land were in possession of Ahmed Hossain and Nur Mohammad. During RS operation, the said land was recorded in their names in RS khatian No. 173 in Plot No. 256. After that, Nur Mohammad gifted his share in the suit plot to his wife, Kewrar Bibi by a registered deed of gift dated 24-4-1980. While jointly possessing 0.51 acre of land, Ahmed Hossain and Kewrar Bibi transferred the same to defendant Nos.4-8 by five registered deeds of sale dated 15-11-1982 and one Shamsul Haque by a registered deed dated 15-12-1982 delivered possession of the suit land to them. After that, Shamsul Haque transferred his 8½ decimals of land to one Fatema Akther by a registered deed dated 29-7-1993. Subsequently, Fatema Akther transferred the same to defendant No. 9 by a registered deed dated 26-4-1995 and defendant Nos. 4-9 mutated their names in respect of their purchased land and had since been paying rent regularly. Defendant Nos. 1 and 2 are land grabbers and defendant No. 1 fraudulently created a registered power of attorney in respect of 58 decimals land out of the total land of CS Plot No. 78 and appointed defendant No. 2 as his attorney. On the strength of said forged power of attorney, the defendants in collusion with some miscreants had been trying to take forcible possession of the suit land from defendant Nos. 4-9. In such a situation, the plaintiffs filed Title Suit No. 168 of 1999 against defendant Nos. 1 and 2 for permanent injunction. In the meantime, defendant No. 1 cancel-led the power of attorney by a registered deed dated 20-1-2000 and the plaintiffs did not get possession of the suit land on the basis of agreement dated 27-7-1999 and the suit being false is liable to be dismissed.
